key_insight: An AI agent can take a prohibited action even when the user’s request is benign and every returned tool statement is true—if a safety-critical fact is missing. EpiSEM-Bench tests how agents handle these evidence gaps.
problem_solved: How can we evaluate whether tool-using agents recognize missing safety evidence, recover needed facts, and respect action boundaries instead of treating incomplete information as permission?
method: Introduce an executable benchmark with 300 matched unsafe/safe task pairs across six domains.
Evaluate agent behavior when tool responses omit safety-relevant facts without providing false statements.
Assess unsafe execution, safety boundaries, and evidence recovery under missing evidence.
impact: EpiSEM-Bench gives practitioners a way to test safety failures caused by incomplete—not necessarily incorrect—tool outputs. It highlights the importance of checking for missing evidence before agents act.
visual_elements: Decision flow: benign request → incomplete tool response → recover evidence or risk unsafe action.
Side-by-side matched safe/unsafe tasks highlighting the safety-critical fact.
Benchmark overview with “300 task pairs” and six domain icons.
Three evaluation icons: unsafe execution, safety boundaries, and evidence recovery.
paper_title: EpiSEM-Bench: Evaluating Safety and Evidence Recovery in LLM Agents under Missing Evidence
paper_authors: Qijin Zhang, Hanzhen Wang, Yuehan Zhao, Haoyu Dai, Yao Shu
